components.name: Mobile Navigation
components.description: A flat paper strip that keeps the map primary on small screens.

narrative.overview: The interface feels like a notebook that is actively used on a trip, not a themed scrapbook. Warm paper, ruled divisions, editorial serif headings, compact date marks, and real visit photography give memories a physical home while the map remains the dominant working surface. The system is calm and information-dense.
keyCharacteristics: Map-first split workspace on desktop and map-plus-bottom-sheet on mobile.
Restrained physical cues: rules, paper tones, date stamps, and attached photographs.
Small-radius rectangular controls; pills only for tags, filters, and people.
Korean editorial serif for memory titles, clear sans-serif for operation.

rules.name: The Functional Ink Rule
rules.body: Vermilion locates or commits, olive classifies, and blue-black communicates; do not swap these roles for decoration.

rules.name: The Paper Majority Rule
rules.body: Warm neutral fields occupy most of every screen so accent colors remain meaningful.

rules.name: The Memory Voice Rule
rules.body: Use the serif face for places, memories, and reflective prose; keep operational text in sans-serif.

rules.name: The Physical Cause Rule
rules.body: A shadow is allowed only when a paper layer is visibly above another surface.

dos: Do let the map and member photographs carry visual interest.
Do use rules and paper tone to establish hierarchy before adding a shadow.
Do keep core controls at least 42px tall and preserve visible keyboard focus.
Do label demonstration content explicitly as synthetic.
donts: Don't introduce glassmorphism, purple gradients, oversized marketing copy, or decorative AI illustrations.
Don't turn every piece of information into a rounded floating card.
Don't use vermilion as ambient decoration; reserve it for location, selection, and commitment.
Don't simulate paper with noisy fake grain; the ruled structure is enough.
